claims.claim: Reviewers mention that enemy placement consists of large hordes and groups scattered across rooms.

citations.review_text:
Presonal Rating: Very Negative (30%)

So I got Scholar via Steam key for roughly 16€, to complete the series. And before you say ''Skill issue'', I'm fresh off beating Dark Souls 3 and halfway in New Game+1 on there.

So, I thought this was actually worthy of a mildly positive review, until I noticed that my HP wasn't full after a few deaths. You lose some amount of HP every time you die. And it has no problem draining you of half your total HP. That means that this game essentialy punishes you for struggling. Yes, a Souls-like PUNISHES you for struggling, by making you struggle EVEN MORE.

The combat itself isn't really bad, but the enemy placement is questionable. Why are there hordes of enemies just scattered across every bigger room? Feels just like a cheap way on how to increase difficulty. Hitboxes don't feel weird, but also aren't anything crazy good.

The graphics, I really thought that it will look better, but it looks worse than DS1 in some places (Sure that one got a remaster, but bro)

The ONLY good that I can think of is the soundtrack back in Majula. It's a decent soundtrack, but that's pretty much it.

Havel spam: a video game (a.k.a. copy-paste tough mobs simulator) 
P.S. I did play through from start to finish in console, hence my disappointment and seemingly never playing it, but do note I never played the DLCs at this point in time

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the Adaptability stat is practically mandatory to level up in order to improve dodge roll invincibility frames and item usage speed, yet the game never explains it.

citations.review_text:
Dark souls 2 is a rough diamond.
In order to make it perfect , 1st you have to change some buttons and make it more similar to elden ring key bindings or ds 3. 
2nd it doesn`t matter what class you pick invest in adaptability until your agility reaches 96 ( usually 20 points in ADP ).
 3rd turn off the double clicking functionality ( it`s really bad).
Now you are ready to face the game challenges and actually enjoy it.
The game has a lot of mechanics better than DS1 but the enemy spawns are ridiculous so get comfortable with it. The lore is detached from dark souls series but it`s beautiful on it`s own.
And finally don`t let Noobs or instagram reels fool you , the game is much easier than it`s believed, just be careful and do the adjustments I said earlier and you understand why some people call this game peak souls 2.

Positives: Great atmosphere, world building, gameplay and character building.

Negatives: Inaccurate hitboxes, dodge roll only works properly when you invest in a stat, ugly character creation, ugly locomotion animations.

I've tried many times to get into Dark Souls 2 and every time It let's me down. Amazing world and fun characters. 
But this game has some of the most awful enemy placements and most egregious runbacks to FromSoft date. The gameplay is slow and clunky. Drinking or consuming items will stop you dead in your tracks. Enemies will have long windups or awkward animations that make learning patterns a snore and frustrating. Bosses suffer the same boring gameplay with longer time to practice and improve because the designers thought you need to clear an entire area just to get back to the fight, which probably left you out of most supplies to properly tackle the boss and the funniest part? This slow, clunky, painful gameplay can all be slightly fixed by leveling up your adp. Actual poo game design to make what was once something you practiced and got better at into a numbers game and makes me waste souls that could've gone to making the game experience better by leveling up stats that actually matter. This games difficulty is frustrating  to play with and not fun to master in the slightest. I don't think I'll ever be able to finish it nor understand where the love from this game comes from.

TLDR.: very bad port, poor quality game, way behind its era's possibilities, heavily overpriced and overrated. 

I might push myself through this game for lore reasons, but do not ever-ever buy this for full price. I wish this was PS exclusive, and Bloodborne had a proper port for PC.

Very bad 1:1 port, feels like a pirated, cracked game. The tooltips were not even updated for PC users, you have to google everything. The game constantly resets some configurations you have to readjust with each game start. Missing this may result in ingame death, which the game actively punishes. Cheating is prohibited as per their EULA, so there's no way to amend your losses caused by their mistakes without risking your account.

Extremely outdated design on all fronts compared to its era, especially for the price. 

Some very bad design choices like Adaptability, an attribute that is basically mandatory to level up, but is never explained

Very clunky, slow animations. If you are curious how a pensioner fight club looks like, this game is for you

Controls are unresponsive too many times, this is an issue on all platforms. Movement has too many rough edges, it's disturbingly hard to control and position your character, especially during fights. Sprinting and rolling on the same button sometimes causes a hiccup where after sprinting and arriving to an object, certain terrain element, or pushing a different button may cause your character to dodge. This of course causes fatal accidents. This group of bugs still exists in Elden Ring, 7 years and 3 games later.

Some collisions are terrible. You're constantly slipping and floating on terrain, and enemies hit through walls. Your hits are the only exception as your theatrical, wide, self-exposing swings are beautifully crafted to be stuck in literally everything.

Sometimes, terrain assets you can interact with like barrels do not reset and certain objects like gates do not stay open after a bonfire rest. This may break progression at t…

Story, weapon system, items, music, every second boss is phenomenal. Some bosses are not as memorable as others though. If you love a grind that gets more rewarding the more you stick to it, this is for you. I had to play it with a game guide though; nothing about leveling or weapon stats are explained by the game. Still, I love this one.

citations.review_text:
If you are a PC player, the hate is warranted. They released a PC version that makes you do research and download mods that break the EULA if you want to use mouse and keyboard. Even after you spend and hour or two figuring this out, the mouse sensitivity will need to be tweaked via your mouse drivers(because the in-game setting is ridiculous) and will never feel right. Controller is only superior if you are playing a flight sim or game with driving in it like GTA so you can utilize the advantages of the joystick so that you don't have to(for example): rapidly tap right to turn slowly instead of cranking it all the way. In Dark Souls, you have the 360 degree angles via your mouse movement and it's way faster/better in every way in this type of game, unless you are laid back on a couch, but this is a PC port... apparently.
I just beat DS1 on mouse/keyboard and loved it. I'm not used to this kind of game on a controller but this basically forces you. I'm used to being able to move the camera or change weapons while running, this game makes it impossible on controller. Some buttons are used for 3 or more functions, like: tapping B is roll/dodge. Holding B is sprint. Holding B to sprint is required to jump by pushing in left joystick. This makes it near impossible to customize the controls to how you want it. 
Also, settings are abysmal in general, not just key mapping. There's no way to change that insane UI scale that is meant for 720p. There's literally 3 things in "screen" settings, including blood settings and brightness. It's absolutely terrible.
I think that's the main reason why this game is such utter trash; the PC-port that did nothing more than make sure it runs. I immediately noticed how far-off it is from DS1, it's bright, there are tons of friendly NPCs around etc. What absolute trash. Clearly released off the back of DS1 to cash in. 
It sucks, I was looking forward to this after DS1. This is the first time I regret dismissing all the warnings about a game…

citations.review_text:
Dark souls 2 is a rough diamond.
In order to make it perfect , 1st you have to change some buttons and make it more similar to elden ring key bindings or ds 3. 
2nd it doesn`t matter what class you pick invest in adaptability until your agility reaches 96 ( usually 20 points in ADP ).

Now you are ready to face the game challenges and actually enjoy it.

And finally don`t let Noobs or instagram reels fool you , the game is much easier than it`s believed, just be careful and do the adjustments I said earlier and you understand why some people call this game peak souls 2.

I see why people hate this game. Its production chaos was well documented and you can tell this was rushed to market. Easy bosses, large mobs of copy paste enemies, story isn't even related to DS1 or 3, ADP is stupid, the lifegem system is stupid, everything is down hill after Majula. Just play 1 and 3 and skip this slop that Miyazaki didn't even work on.

4K mod + unlocked FPS makes this a great throwback to a Dark Souls classic. I remember when DS2 first came out and immediately thinking, there’s no way this was made by the same team that made Dark Souls 1. The game constantly mistakes difficulty for good design-like throwing 7 enemies at you at once and assuming, “Well, that’s harder, so it must be more Dark Souls.” But that completely misses what made DS1, and later DS3, so special. Those games were challenging because of thoughtful enemy placement, level design, atmosphere, and encounters that felt brutal but fair. DS2 too often just feels difficult for the sake of being difficult. Still, a classic. 


Overall: 8/10

Yes.. It's quite ganky. After how easy it was to skip most levels in DS1, DS2 has the expectation that you'll be proceeding through levels carefully, and it was an extremely unpopular choice. That's why DS3, Bloodborne, Sekiro, and Elden Ring ignored this change and went back to DS1 easy running. 

If you engage with this game the same way you do with the others, you WILL hate it. You have to slowly clear levels front to back, instead of rushing the next bonfire and working your way backwards from it. You aren't allowed that safety net in DS2. Does that mean levels take longer? Yes. That's why there are lifegems and life regeneration equipment. To offset that difficulty and time investment.

I'm not entirely defending that choice, however. Some areas like the Earthen Peak and Iron Keep are like an actual joke of game design. The sheer amount of enemies that are stuffed into small rooms or narrow corridors eventually turned my rage into apathy as I gave up on good level design during these moments. Both of these levels I just gave up on playing normally and chose to rely on the permadeath feature (kill and enemy ~12 times and they stop respawning) to make my way through the annoying spaces.

Also, ADP. It's objectively a stupid stat. But you can smash 15 or so points into it early on and you don't have to worry about i-frames or the flask drinking speed again. You get levels really easily in this game, and if it bothers you so much that you refuse to fight anything before getting proper i-frames, go cheese Dragonrider and you can get it done within minutes of starting. Is it a stupid chore? Yes. But the amount of talk about ADP you hear online, I thought it was an irredeemable blemish on this game. It's really not.

If you like DS1, you'll likely enjoy this one too if you make adjustments to your expectations. Also, maybe spoil yourself a bit on the early game. There are some shortcuts amd bonfire placements you might miss if you play completely blind, and you'll kic…

Dark Slop 2 is a great example of a company tryna make a game without the developer who made the game good in the first place. Pure slop, and calling this game slop is an understatement. No progression in terms of armour as you progress through the game (I've had the same armour equipped since the 2-3rd area you progress through and I'm 12 areas deep, absolutely shocking. Every enemy either has the attack speed of Bruce Lee on speed, a million poison attacks or the power of Thor turned to the max. Area NPC enemies are more difficult than the bosses are, and to top it off, you have to grind out the first 20 odd levels for dodging to actually function so good luck making a good build until your level 110+. Gank squads are just total bs, you can't fight a single enemy without his mate 9 miles away legging it to your fight to fist you from behind, I guess that's what the 2 means, as every fight is a 2v1. Got this game on sale and I even regret paying the sale price, absolute aids

cohorts.summary: Midway reviewers adjust to punishing systems, aggressive enemy pursuits, and sprawling hub layouts.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the adaptability stat affects dodge roll i-frames, and investing points in it is necessary to make dodging feel responsive.

citations.review_text:
Overall I enjoyed Dark souls II, I disliked some of the mid-later game content. it seemed they reused boss fight assets and that felt lazy to me. to get the game to feel like the first one you must increase a skill to increase i frames. however, dark souls II is very forgiving with giving the player a lot of souls so it wasn't the end of the world just more annoying than anything. 

I played it and enjoyed it. Would I immediatley jump back in to play it over again? No. give it a few years then i may jump back in to see what the old game was like but that's it.

overall score: solid 7/10.

Too many enemies, terrible hitboxes, and the game expects you to level ADP just to get normal i-frames. Having to invest 25 ADP before dodging feels responsive is ridiculous. The combat can be frustrating rather than challenging, especially when you’re getting hit by attacks that look like they should have missed. DS2 has some good ideas, but these mechanics make the experience unnecessarily annoying.
The game would be better if i-frames and carry load were not a separate stat.

Dark Souls II opts for a hub-and-spoke approach rather than Dark Souls' nested world design, so players looking to recreate that experience may be a little disappointed. However, DS2 is easily one of the prettiest games in the series, with some really dream-like worlds that are incredibly varied and a lot of fun to explore. It definitely has some... odd design choices (namely ADP, which you want to level to 24 to have decent dodge rolls) and the controls feel a little clunky at times, but I've been really enjoying the game so far.

I say so far because this game is massive compared to Dark Souls. I'm enjoying taking my time with it and really exploring the world, there are a lot of secrets to uncover. I recommend running the Lighting Engine Mod if you can, as it supports HDR and up-to-date lighting, which really makes the game and torch mechanics shine (literally)

Couple of tips if you're playing this for the first time. Get the ADP stat up to around 96, my buddy told me to go for 99 personally. 
ADP affects i-frames, the frames that allows you to not be hit during dodge rolls and the base i-frames in DS2 is lower than DS1 and DS3, having 96 is basically the same i-frame as they use in DS1 and DS3. Honestly get this as soon as possible, you can probably also play with lower ADP, but if you want it similiar to DS1 and DS3, go for that. 

If you decide to parry, do know the parrying in DS2 is different. 
Personally I didn't get a hang of it and it annoyed me, especially after DS1 which is very much a parrying game.
So I just skipped parrying in DS2, and honestly it's fine, DS2 imo is more of a lock-on and dodge game, while DS1 had 4 ways to dodge (left, right, back, forward), DS2 has 8 way movement, meaning you can dodge forward left, forward right etc. 

Dodging feels really good in DS2, while parrying feels just weird. 
Parrying feels really good in DS1, while dodging usually still gets you hit.

Otherwise this game is not deserving of its bad reputation. It's quite fun actually.
Jankanator movement & game is addicting, upgrade adp

So much pain but so much fun.
DS2 is vastly different from DS1 in a lot of ways. Controls feel a little more clunky, leveling up ADP for better dodging/rolling, the hollow status effects just to name a few. Some may think that these add "artificial" difficulty but I thought the game gave you more than enough to conquer the areas and bosses. 
As far as difficulty goes, I personally felt it was a little more difficult than DS1 but still fair. I will agree with others about enemy placement especially in NG+ and beyond, areas were pretty inflated with enemies and I thought most of the challenge was just trying to survive long enough to get to the boss or a bonfire. Of course practice makes perfect and learning the areas, the enemies, your build, and how to use your gems/estus you'll eventually adapt and overcome.
The bosses were pretty neat. There were some forgettable ones and some of them become enemies later on in the game which was a bit annoying but for the most part they were all a good time. The lore behind them tied into the story very well. The DLC bosses were probably the best bosses in the game in my opinion (except the gank squad, you know what I'm talking about...)
Overall, it's a good time. I would definitely recommend this if you're coming from DS1 or just looking for a unique souls-like experience. Just take it slow, learn the mechanics, and explore the world. I wouldn't consider myself very good at these types of games but I still had a blast, even if it took a toll on my sanity. You will not be disappointed.
I do want end off on saying this game is online by default. From what I know there is no way to switch it to offline mode in the game unless you adjust settings in windows defender firewall. This is the only way I know so you can get achievements on Steam while being offline. Anyways go say hi to the Emerald Herald.

I actually played all the dark souls games in addition to demon souls, bloodborne and elden ring, including all the dlc’s for each game on PlayStation before I permanently moved over to PC and sold my PS5, and dark souls 2 has to be one of my favourites out of the lot, it’s my favourite one out of the dark souls trilogy, even though that can be a controversial opinion amongst dark souls fans! This play through on the PC was my second play through and I used to it kill every boss in the game and really enjoyed playing through it the second time and exploring all the areas and what seemed quite open world at first became more linear once you become familiar with the areas, unlike elden ring which would be a true open world game in comparison. Dark souls 2 is more like elden ring in the sense of all the equipment and various builds you can get out of it, compared to the other ones, and gives that vibe of a early rendition of what elden ring was to be. The addition of the adaptability stat is what makes it feel clunky at first until you level it up to about mid 20-s-30’s to make it feel more like the other games when dodging. It’s one of those games that when you get the hang of it, it’s really hard to put down, and you don’t realise how and where the time has gone when you get stuck into it, and next thing you know, you’re going to have little sleep to wake up for work in the morning!

Overall 9.5/10 and I can’t wait for the next proper souls single player game from FromSoftware!

It's the weakest of the Dark Souls trilogy, but it's still a game that's worth your time to play if you like the genre.

The level design is a pretty noticeable step down from Dark Souls 1. It lacks the brilliant interconnected world design of the first game, and a lot of the placement of the areas and enemies/bosses within those areas feels kind of artificial. The game has a lot of bad enemy placements being full of terrible ganks, that feel much more like artificial difficulty than the carefully crafted challenged one would hope for from this genre.

That said, I still had a lot of fun exploring DS2's world, it has a lot of locations that leave a pretty lasting impression, and the level design is noticeably better in the game's DLCs (included in this game, no extra purchase).

-------------------------------

Unfortunately, the bosses are mostly very underwhelming in this game, with there being lots of very similar "big guy in armor" fights, and the fights that don't fall in to this category being largely very awkward. There are some definite highlights, particularly in the DLC, but the average boss quality is pretty low. There are also pretty awful boss runbacks for the majority of the game's bosses. 

-------------------------------

ADP is the other big criticism of this game. Just make sure to level it somewhat frequently, and it won't be an issue, it's only really a problem if you don't know about it.

-------------------------------

Overall, I had a pretty good time with this game, but I think it is riddled with major flaws that can be a turn off for some people.

I know that Dark Souls 2 is widely considered the worst in the franchise, and while yes I do have issues with the game, to call it the *worst* is pure nonsense. I would honestly much rather play DS2 over DS1 any day of the week, and that includes the remaster they came out with shortly after DS2 came out. 

Now, will I say that Dark Souls 2 is flawless? Absolutely not. Dark Souls 2 has plenty of issues. Some of the hitboxes are kind of weird, but that only happens if you do not level the adapability stat. The only exception I can think of to where that doesn't happen is with Fume Knight, and he's already ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ as is. but if you have the Scholar of The First Sin edition (the version I played) a lot of the issues are kinda just... gone. 

It took me 31 hours to beat the game, mostly because of Fume Knight eating up most of my boss attempts while going through the game. If you like the Soulslike genre, definitely play it. If this is your first Souls game... well then that's a different story. Definetly play the other games first BEFORE coming to this, because if you do start off with this game, you are going to hate it. 

Dark Souls 2 was the last game in my journey from playing all the souls games. It ranks up there in my top three, with Bloodborne in first, Dark Souls 2 in second, and Elden Ring and Dark Souls 3 being interchangeable.

A great game, but not quite as good as Dark Souls 1.

There is a large variety of viable builds, and every weapon I tried had a good moveset. The DLC areas are amazing, and have some of my favorite bosses in the series.

There are some terribly designed areas that are a slog to get through, namely Iron Keep and Shrine of Amana. The final boss is too easy, and is one of three boss fights that take place in the same arena.

Overall, I rate it 8/10.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that enemies aggressively pursue the player across long distances, preventing players from simply running past them.

citations.review_text:
Dark Souls 2 doesn't quite capture the magic of the original, though it certainly has great moments.

From the very moment you load in you feel that something is off. Movement feels sluggish, the camera movement is non-linear and the animations look odd.

On the gameplay side of things, this game retains many fun elements of the original, however, the main challenge in this game comes from the quantity of enemies, rather than the quality. The game is much less about learning movesets and fighting through a gauntlet of one or two strong enemies at a time. Instead it's more about learning enemy placement and skirting around their their huge aggro ranges in order to not get ganked to death. Constant meticulous aggro management is the name of the game. Meanwhile bosses felt anticlimactic and they are much easier compared to other souls games. The strange way difficulty is created in this game is just not always terribly enjoyable. I will say this becomes less of a problem as you progress, and you no longer have to suffer through endless hordes of chaff on 100 HP and a single estus charge.

it's not a bad game by any means, and it does improve on some aspects like class building and the equipment upgrading process. The world is absolutely gorgeous and memorable and I certainly wouldn't recommend any souls fans to skip this installment, which is something I've seen people say online.

In summary, I'll give it a recommend, just know that it has some quirks that take some adjusting to, and especially the early game can feel bit rough in a bad way. But if you stick with it, it develops into another fantastic Souls experience.

I played all Dark Souls games in the series and, whatever people may say, Dark Souls II was the game I had the most fun with. I couldn't stop playing or thinking about this game. When I went to bed, I was playing the game in my dreams or planning my next strategies. Dark Souls II is the hardest game in the series. NPCs always follow you to the end, there are too many of them, and they can be really tough to beat. Bosses are the most difficult and most enjoyable in the series. Even the game mechanics themselves want you to die. But the more difficult it gets as the game constantly does a skill check, the more cautious and better you become, and the more enjoyment you get from your achievements. I feel sad for people who have never even tried this game. The way Dark Souls games are meant to be played in order is DS1 - DS2 - DS3, but I see a lot of people who just start playing the series with DS3, and they are ruining this beautiful series for themselves. I've also seen a lot of people just skip Dark Souls II and play Dark Souls III. Please don't do that. Just give it a try. I had also heard bad things about this game, but I was skeptical and gave it a try regardless. The only thing that I can say is that it was one of the best decisions I've ever made. With Gavlan, you wheel? You deal! The existence of Gavlan alone is enough to make this game a masterpiece.

This game does not deserve the hate that it receives in the community, I'm thoroughly having fun with this one. I can't help but think those people were just trying to run past everyone while simultaneously aggravating all of the enemies.

It's alright. A fair bit clunkier than the other games which takes some getting used to. Just a fair warning though, enemies will almost never stop following you, so if you pull the good ol' classic "just run through the common enemies" you'll be mauled within seconds if you stop.

So so much better than Demon's Souls. While the  bosses were insanely easy except for Red Smelter Demon, Fume Knight (goated), Darklurker, and maaaybe Velstadt. Everything was fun to dodge and not nearly as mindless as people give them credit for. Most bosses I beat in like 3 tries but they were still fun and enjoyable. The world design is.. weird. Kinda interconnected, kinda not, and the choice to have the Forest and Tower of Flame both lead to the same singular branching path dead end was an odd choice.

It looks great, plays great, gameplay feels less janky than fromsoft's previous two games, and in some ways it feels like it does some things even better than ds1. Weapons and armor rarely ever break cause they repair themselves at bonfires, flasks are nerfed but you have lifegems which are like demons souls grass heals, and runbacks... aren't bad at all! The only ones I struggled with at all was really just the old iron king, and that's only cause I didn't know about the secret bonfire right next to the arena until after the fight. Sir Alonne was 2 rooms and blue smelter was 3 rooms, like wtf how do people complain this much about these, ds1 was way way way worse (frigid outskirts sucked tho). People prolly run through the levels and have the entire area's enemy count chasing them to the fog gate then complain about "bad game", but you as a player should EASILY be able to tell when you can run past to the gate and when you should fight your way through one-by-one, it's communicated insanely well to the player and I think souls fans are just dummy dums.

Overall it felt like a streamlined, pretty darn fun and consistent souls game. One of the weaker entries sure, but gosh is it still good and worth a playthrough.

The difficulty is more "hey lets throw a bunch of really annoying enemies in a tight spot" instead of fun and challenging mechanically. That said, I overall enjoyed my play through with the exception of the old iron king and sunken king DLC. Those are hot garbage and you should avoid them. The Ivory King DLC is a little annoying since you need to play through it twice really and it contains what is probably the absolute worst area in all of Dark Souls, however its an optional area. The Sunken King DLC also contains what is probably the worst boss fight in all of souls as well along with the worst run back to said boss, yes, worse than Bed of Chaos. Again, that is also an optional area/boss. But I still had fun playing it and its not a bad game. Im actually playing through NG+ right now. Weapon selection is great and armor variety is too. As nonsensical as some of the world layout is, I felt like I enjoyed the brighter, more colorful kingdom of Drangleic and its surrounding areas. I picked this up for $15, so definetely wait for a sale.

Oh boy. DS2.

Majula definitely looks great. I personally think this had some of the most forgettable bosses amongst the other games in the series though, and wish they hooked into me like the bosses in DS1 did. Overall same gameplay loop with boss runbacks and having to learn the fights patterns. Would recommend as a filler game, but this didn't do much for me this time around.

Dark Souls 2 is the black sheep of the Souls series. 

DS2 is such a weird "souls" game but it is still a good game, it feels different from the other souls game. Yes the gameplay can be little clunky and slow, the runback is atrocious, it has a lot of mobs and the bosses aren't that memorable. But it still feels like a such a special game despite all that. There is something quite magical in the "flaws". The areas and settings are fun to explore and there is a lot of variety. The DLCs also are quite good. 

In terms of difficulty, the game isn't that hard especially since the bosses are actually really easy, especially if you come from more modern fromsoft games where the bosses has more complex moveset. Dark Souls 2 bosses are so simple in terms of moveset and easy to predict. The struggle are more in the areas and runbacks.

The atmosphere in this game is almost as good as Dark Souls 1 IMO. Majula is the best hub of all video games. It is so peaceful and beautiful.

Despite the apparent flaws of the game, there is something magical in it i can't quite explain.

Dark Souls 2 is a frustrating game that tests your patience at almost every turn. It has the hallmark things that made Dark Souls a great game, but they also threw ♥♥♥♥ at the fan to see what sticks, to varying degrees of success. The result is an uneven game that is still mostly good but has parts that really don't work. The benefit is they learned from their mistakes on this game and future games are better for it. But it leaves this game in an awkward position, a good game with glaring flaws that are impossible to ignore, to the point where I can't really recommend it to everyone. But if you are a Soulslike fan, it's a really interesting and mostly good game. 

The biggest issues I have with the game, are the runbacks, which are some of the worst in the entire genre. The durability system is frustrating and adds nothing. And in general the game is maybe too esoteric and confusing for its own good. Pull out a guide with no shame.

cohorts.summary: Long-term players continue to navigate sluggish healing animations and awkward control bindings.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the PC version lacks proper keyboard and mouse UI prompts, defaulting entirely to controller icons and featuring problematic key bindings such as forced mouse double-clicks.

citations.review_text:
[h2] The hate is valid. [/h2]

It has a few novel mechanics like bonfire ascetics and the torch that are quite intresting. But the combat, you know, the thing you will be doing for a majority of the time, is just horrible. With the exception of maybe 3 bosses all of the are mechanically boring having at most 3 moves and can super easily be baited into performing the same one that gives you the largest window to attack. The easy areas are childishly easy while the "hard" ones feature excessive enemy spam of the worst enemies. 

I played with keyboard and mouse which i would not recommend. ALL onscreen prompts are for a controller. The default keybinds are disgusting and it feels like someone who has never touched a keyboard came up with them, rebinding is a must if you do not want to go hollow. I would rather have keyboard only (without mouse) controlls than dealing with the default keybindings (I have done this for ds1 and it works suprisingly well). One of the defaults is double klick for heavy attack which (I have not looked that much into it) makes it so there is about a 0.5s delay between clicking the mouse and the character reacting. unique keys for every action is a requirement from the game, it will not allow two actions to share a key even if there is no ambiguity in which should be preformed. 

The only parts i enjoyed were the the absolute beginning, scrounging for resources, the last portion of the game after you've gotten the ring (but not the boss before credits), and the DLC which is very good.

I have heard rumors that the original ds2 actually featured a somewhat decent difficulty curve and actual intention behind enemy placements. If you really want to play ds2 you should probably get that version NOT scholar of the first sin.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that healing items like the Estus Flask take significantly longer to consume and activate compared to other titles in the series.

citations.review_text: After over 150+ hours of playtime in DS2 I can definitively say this game is another great entry in the dark souls trilogy. I will list all major issues I have with the game and then follow up with the pros. First off I can not understand why the developers made invasions such a big part of the game and do not even get me started with the hitboxes. It is one of the worst parts of the game in my opinion and they only add to the fire in New Game+. The estus takes way too long to actually drink and then fully activate. It is a nerf coming from DS1. This game has 2 of the worst areas in all of From Software history being Shrine of Amana and Frigid Outskirts. After beating DS1 and coming to this game almost all of the bosses in the first half of the game are way too easy. The DLCs really do carry in terms of bosses. The lighting in this game (especially Majula) is weird when compared to other games. Those are most of the gripes I have with this game. And now for the pros. I absolutely love the outfits in this game. There are so many great outfits with crazy aura that I can not choose a favorite. Bonfire ascetics were an amazing addition as they allow you to fight your favorite boss as many times as you want. While the bosses in the latter half of the game are well executed, they are safe. Not crazy innovative or breath taking. The variety of weapons and spells adds so much depth and replayability. The gameplay feels very smooth and fresh when compared to DS1. Solid 7.5/10 for me would recommend.

Like a lot of players, I went from hating this entry in the series to absolutely loving it. Definitely grows on you over time and I developed an appreciation for what it does so differently from the 1 and 3 over the years, despite healing flask animations taking as long as an afternoon nap. lol
It's the most bleak in tone and you can really feel the oppressiveness of the world. The game is merciless. Even irritating at times with how cryptic it can be, but it's all worth it just for Majula alone. Probably the best hub world in any souls game. I'm not the most skilled player and admittedly the game got a lot easier for me after I looked up a few things on YouTube to try and understand some of its unique mechanics and gain some advantages over some of the tougher areas. Only mod I'd personally recommend is the DS2LightingEngine mod. It's literally night and day compared to vanilla render. Fixes one of the most common critiques of the game when it released(how bland the OG lighting was).

claims.claim: Reviewers state that character movement is locked to an 8-directional grid, which conflicts poorly with the lock-on combat system.

citations.review_text:
The level design ranges from mediocre to offensive, the bosses are some of the most phoned-in, anticlimactic fights in any game I've ever played, and even things as simple as the movement are botched, due to the weird 8-directional grid that your character is locked to.

The adage that DS2 is a good game, but a bad Dark Souls game is, I think, exceedingly generous. If DS2 had to stand on its own without borrowing the Dark Souls title, it would be largely forgotten.

i have finally achieved the dark soul.

all achievements... i am free again... =' )

This game definitely deserves the hate it gets. If anyone disagrees with you or attempts to explain the nuances of why its actually good - politely smile and nod along with them until they leave the room, they have serious mental deficiencies.

The lock-on combat system does NOT pair well with the 8 directional dead zone movement controls. This is by far my biggest complaint and its honestly so bad its hilarious.

Enemies can and will hit you through the wall. Accept that. Make peace with it. It will happen.

Enemy placement is god-awful, I'm looking at you Iron Keep. This issue is amplified by some of the worst boss run-backs in the franchise. *cough* *cough* BOTH SMELTER DEMONS *cough* *cough*

However, it has its own charm. Its the black sheep of the franchise, but I only recommend it so you can commiserate with the rest of us <3.

citations.review_text:
[h2] The hate is valid. [/h2]

It has a few novel mechanics like bonfire ascetics and the torch that are quite intresting. But the combat, you know, the thing you will be doing for a majority of the time, is just horrible. With the exception of maybe 3 bosses all of the are mechanically boring having at most 3 moves and can super easily be baited into performing the same one that gives you the largest window to attack. The easy areas are childishly easy while the "hard" ones feature excessive enemy spam of the worst enemies. 

I played with keyboard and mouse which i would not recommend. ALL onscreen prompts are for a controller. The default keybinds are disgusting and it feels like someone who has never touched a keyboard came up with them, rebinding is a must if you do not want to go hollow. I would rather have keyboard only (without mouse) controlls than dealing with the default keybindings (I have done this for ds1 and it works suprisingly well). One of the defaults is double klick for heavy attack which (I have not looked that much into it) makes it so there is about a 0.5s delay between clicking the mouse and the character reacting. unique keys for every action is a requirement from the game, it will not allow two actions to share a key even if there is no ambiguity in which should be preformed. 

The only parts i enjoyed were the the absolute beginning, scrounging for resources, the last portion of the game after you've gotten the ring (but not the boss before credits), and the DLC which is very good.

I have heard rumors that the original ds2 actually featured a somewhat decent difficulty curve and actual intention behind enemy placements. If you really want to play ds2 you should probably get that version NOT scholar of the first sin.
